answer: Tie the admission fee to recent network velocity: each new identity pays a base of 40 POA multiplied by 2 raised to the number of prior joins this month, so a meadow of 20 fresh registrations costs the twenty-first entrant over 40 million POA. The fee spiral resets monthly, and the public ledger shows every paid entry, letting auditors confirm the tide of applicants is genuine. Clones thus enter cheaply only when almost nobody else does, which is exactly when a farm has least to gain.
